title: Strategy session and capture the flag
materials: Cones or lights for the boundary
Glow sticks for flags and players if outdoors
One plan sheet and pencil per patrol

displayContent.headline: Plan, play, review
displayContent.body: 8 minutes to plan. Write it all on one sheet.
points: Commander’s intent: one sentence. How do we win?
Roles: attack, defense, scout, jail guard
A fallback if the flag carrier is tagged

prompts.text: After-action review: What was supposed to happen? What actually happened? Why was there a difference? What will we do differently next time?
prompts.answer: Each patrol answers all four, then revises its plan for round 2.

prompts.text: Final review: did your change work?
prompts.answer: Compare round 1 and round 2. That revision is the part that meets the requirement’s “what improvements could be used next time.”

leaderScript: Plan (8 min): each patrol writes its plan on one sheet, using the four points on screen.
Play round 1 (7 min): two-hand touch, a jail on each side, flags visible.
Press → for the after-action review. Patrols answer the four questions and revise their plan.
Press → for the final review: did the change work?
Light: in Independence the sun sets about 5:06 p.m. in mid-November. Play in a gym, or outdoors with glow sticks on flags and players, a lit boundary, and buddy pairs.
ifShortOnTime: Protect this block. Cut the rank race first.
lowVolunteerNote: Two adults are better for safety outdoors in the dark: one at each end of the field.
